title: Clo Brazil Workshop Highlights
description:
We are very happy to share with you the best moments of our first in-person Workshop in Brazil!

We held this event in partnership with the Centro Universitário Belas Artes, at Campus Cidade Jardins, in São Paulo. During four intensive days, we had the unique opportunity to teach our students in person, and the results were incredible!

Would you like to participate in a Workshop offered by the CLO Brasil team?

Fill out our interest form and be the first to know about upcoming courses: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/1-FyCPeFnb3DlEGdqEpUH0jbrx2sd38jDrtsp0yelhQY/edit

See you soon!
transcript: Clow is already a software for the fashion industry, so we have tools to think, to weave. I came to the workshop, I have my expectations up there, I learned a lot for the first day and let's see how it will be in the next few days. The face-to-face workshop is something that we have been wanting to do for some time, because we did two virtual workshops, we had a very good acceptance from the community. We pointed out with the Belas Artes partnership, so we used all the infrastructure that they have here, the campus of Cidade Jardim. It was a very beautiful experience, precisely because 3D is starting here in the fashion area in Brazil and we are experiencing a revolution together with the Claw software and being able to see and be part of this moment in which people are learning the software. And using it to improve their knowledge in the fashion area and develop themselves, both in the industry and as freelancers, it is being very gratifying for all of us. We finally arrived on the last day of the course and my expectations were more than met. I loved it. At first I thought the software would be a little difficult, but I realized that it is super intuitive and that you can learn very quickly. I was very happy to have developed so many pieces in such a short time. In four days I practically developed a capsule collection, the top part, the bottom part and even the male part. And this workshop was an incredible experience so that we could have face-to-face contact with our students, with our users and see personally how the software tools motivate people to always learn more, get out of the comfort zone, for different things and new technologies.
markdown_content: ## Overview of Clo Software and Workshop Purpose This section introduces Clo, a specialized software for the fashion industry that offers tools for design and weaving. It also outlines the goals and context of the in-person workshop, emphasizing its role in advancing 3D fashion technology in Brazil. Clo is a software solution designed specifically for the fashion industry, providing tools for designing and weaving garments in a virtual 3D environment. The in-person workshop was organized after two successful virtual sessions, aiming to deepen user engagement and skill development. Hosted in partnership with Belas Artes at the Cidade Jardim campus, the workshop leveraged local infrastructure to foster a collaborative and immersive learning experience. The emergence of 3D technology in Brazil's fashion sector is framed as a transformative revolution, with Clo at the forefront. This workshop allowed participants to directly interact with the software and each other, facilitating knowledge exchange and skill enhancement. The hands-on environment helped users improve their expertise in both industrial fashion design and freelance work, marking a significant milestone in the adoption of digital tools in the region. ## Participant Experience and Learning Outcomes This section summarizes participant feedback on the usability of Clo and the productivity gains achieved during the workshop, highlighting the software’s intuitive interface and rapid learning curve. Attendees reported that Clo exceeded their expectations, particularly regarding ease of use and learning speed. Initially perceived as potentially complex, the software proved highly intuitive, enabling quick mastery of its functionalities. Over the course of four days, participants developed multiple garments, effectively creating a capsule collection including tops, bottoms, and men's wear. The workshop fostered motivation among users to explore new technologies and step beyond their comfort zones. Direct interaction with instructors and peers enhanced the learning process, making the experience both productive and inspiring. This face-to-face format was instrumental in building a community around Clo, strengthening user engagement and encouraging continuous professional development in 3D fashion design.
